Liquidity risk: The Group manages liquidity risk by projecting cash flows, monitoring balance sheet liquidity ratios, and maintaining debt financing plans. Undiscounted contractual maturities of financial liabilities are disclosed.
Market risk: The Group is exposed to currency risk (primarily Euro and US dollars), commodity price risk (coffee), and interest rate risk (long-term borrowings with variable rates).

Currency risk: The Group has exposure to Euro (net statement of financial position exposure of 0.09 crore as at March 31, 2026). Sensitivity analysis shows a 1% movement in Euro impacts profit or loss by 1.49 crore.

Commodity price risk: The Company hedges coffee price using forward commodity contracts based on a 12-month forecast. The company is not exposed to any commodity risk as at March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025.

Interest rate risk: The Group's main interest rate risk arises from long-term borrowings with variable rates. The Group had entered into interest rate swap to hedge the interest rate risk. As at March 31, 2026 and 2025, there were no variable rate instruments exposed to interest rate risk.
Capital management risk: Breaches in meeting financial covenants attached to interest-bearing loans and borrowings would permit the bank to immediately call loans and borrowings.

outlook.statement: Global growth projected at 2.6% (World Bank) and 3.1% (IMF) for 2026; coffee demand resilient with premiumization trends; hospitality recovery supported by leisure travel and business mobility. India GDP grew 7.4% in FY2025-26, projected 6.8-7.2% for FY2026-27. Indian coffee market projected CAGR ~8.9% through 2028, out-of-home segment 15-20% annually. Hospitality sector growth driven by domestic tourism, business travel, MICE revival.

Government initiatives aimed at improving tourism infrastructure, strengthening connectivity, promoting domestic and international tourism, facilitating investments and encouraging sustainable development are expected to provide a strong foundation for the continued growth of India's hospitality industry. These policy measures, coupled with favourable demographic trends and increasing travel demand, are likely to create significant opportunities for organised hospitality players over the long term.

The Company remains focused on strengthening its operational resilience through prudent risk management practices, diversified revenue streams, digital transformation, sustainable business practices and continuous enhancement of guest experiences. Its emphasis on operational excellence, employee capability development, technology adoption, cost optimisation and strong governance enables the Company to effectively manage emerging risks while capitalising on long-term growth opportunities in the hospitality sector.
The Unused Losses will start expiring from FY 27-28. As per the projection, the company will be making sufficient Profit in the coming years to adjust the future deferred Tax Liability.
